question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize request (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, empty capabilities, clientInfo public-agents-researcher 1.0); Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream, MCP-Protocol-Version 2025-06-18

headers.www-authenticate: scheme Bearer, then four parameters: realm Service, error invalid_request, error_description "The access token was not found.", and resource_metadata naming https://mcp.box.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource

decoded.body: empty, zero bytes, on both path forms
decoded.path-forms: the /mcp path form (https://mcp.box.com/mcp) answers the identical status and the identical challenge in the same second, so the documented root endpoint and the conventional path behave the same
decoded.protected-resource-document: 200, 406 bytes: resource https://mcp.box.com/, resource_name "Box Model Context Protocol Server", authorization_servers [https://api.box.com/], bearer_methods_supported [header], resource_documentation https://developer.box.com/guides/box-mcp/remote/ (which answers 200), resource_policy_uri and resource_tos_uri both https://www.box.com/legal/termsofservice
decoded.everything-else-401: every other path of mcp.box.com this probe touched answers 401 with an empty body: the path-aware protected-resource URI /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp, /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, and /.well-known/public-agents.json. The registry's ownership check on this host therefore cannot distinguish absence from refusal
decoded.rest-path: GET https://api.box.com/2.0/users/me with no Authorization header answers 401, zero bytes, with the same challenge minus the resource_metadata parameter
decoded.vendor-claim: the vendor's guide documents OAuth and an administrator-created credential and names no keyless tier, so this refusal is what its own documentation predicts

finding: With no credential on 2026-10-20 at 18:33:58.945Z, the hosted Box MCP server answers an MCP initialize with 401 and an empty body at both https://mcp.box.com and https://mcp.box.com/mcp, carrying an RFC 9728 challenge that names one protected-resource document; that document answers 200 at 406 bytes and names api.box.com as its only authorization server. Every other path of the host, including the path-aware resource URI and the registry's own ownership file, answers 401 with an empty body, so on this host an absent file and a refused one look the same. The REST API refuses the same way. The entry's cells (noAccountNeeded false, auth oauth) are what this measures, and the vendor documents no keyless tier to look for. One IP is one sample.
